D13·ddkn — 2026-09-16
rule: Every fix session of an improvement cycle — loop or baseline — launches through `evaluator fix` on an APPROVED loss row from a refless export of one commit; the baseline's budget is the loop's full cost, no rep is selected by hidden-test score, and a comparison with any unequal parameter yields no verdict.
chose: 3.3 contract — the EQUAL-BUDGET DIRECT-FIX BASELINE, settled before code. (1) ONE RUN MODE FOR BOTH ARMS: `evaluator fix` in ~/IO/sofar-evaluator is how any fix session in a cycle is launched — the baseline arm `direct-fix` and the loop's arm `loop-fix` alike. Same agent binary through the same sandbox shim, same model/effort/timeout, same D12 caps and ledger, same cell construction, same result capture. The arms differ in the PROMPT ONLY: direct-fix gets the loss row and the fix instruction; loop-fix gets exactly that plus the loop's brief (`--brief <file>`, sha256 recorded). run.json records every parameter and `evaluator compare` refuses a verdict when base commit, loss hash, model, effort, timeout, reps, pin, evaluator commit or the row text differ between the two arms. (2) THE LOSS IS THE APPROVED ROW, VERBATIM: `--loss <candidate-hash> --repo <sofar clone>`. The evaluator reads the scope initiative's events.jsonl itself (JSON, no sofar binary — D9 §1 is about results, this is input), requires a `suggestion_proposed` for the hash whose LAST transition is `suggestion_approved` (a rejected, reverted or merely recorded row is refused), and renders the row text from the proposed payload (signal, scope, count, 2.2 trust numbers) plus every cited evidence event (id, ts, type, payload text). Both arms receive byte-identical row text; its sha256 is in every result. (3) THE COMPARATOR IS HIDDEN BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE FIX IS MADE FROM A COMMIT: the cell is a `git archive` of `--base <commit>` into a fresh `git init` repo with one commit — no refs, reflog or objects beyond that tree, so the human r1-fixes change is unreachable through git. The kernel profile denies reads of the source repo and every worktree of it (`git worktree list`) plus any `--hide <path>`, alongside the D9 sealed set; a read probe against each hidden path joins the self-test. After the session the transcript is scanned for `--hidden-term`s (default: `r1-fixes` and every hidden path); a hit VOIDS the attempt — recorded, not packed. Stated limit (D9 §10): the network is open and origin carries the branch, so the scan catches the name, not content fetched under another name. (4) SAME FEEDBACK, NAMED: what either arm may use during its session is the candidate's own suite inside the cell (`npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, the build) and nothing from the evaluator — no hidden tests, no scores, no controls; the kernel denies both arms the same sealed set. Deviations from this feedback set are a new Decision. (5) NO SELECTION WITH HIDDEN-ANSWER ACCESS: one session per rep; the candidate is the cell's HEAD after `git add -A && commit` at session end, packed by `pack` from the cell (candidate identity stays the artifact, D9 §5); EVERY rep is packed and scored; the arm score is the mean over reps; nobody — agent, evaluator, operator — picks a rep by its hidden-test score. (6) EQUAL SPEND MEANS THE LOOP'S FULL SPEND: the loop arm runs FIRST; its full fix-stage cost = its fix launches charged per D12 + its cost outside the evaluator (`tune`, `suggest`, replay, the operator's own sessions), which `compare` takes as `--loop-extra-usd <n>` — required, 0 allowed, never assumed. The baseline's `--max-usd` must be ≥ that full cost, its `--max-launches` = the same reps; compare checks the inequality and WITHHOLDS the verdict when it fails. Stated limit: caps bound launches, not what one `claude -p` session spends inside itself, so actual charged spend of both arms is printed beside the caps and an overspending baseline never helps the loop (a baseline that wins at any budget defeats the loop; a loop that spent past the baseline's cap gets no verdict). (7) VERDICT: KEEP only if the loop arm's mean hidden-test pass on the evaluator's workload is STRICTLY greater than the baseline's at a baseline budget ≥ the loop's full cost; a tie or a loss is DISCARD; a missing eval run, a voided rep or an unequal parameter is WITHHELD with the reason. compare also prints any `--also <candidate>` (the human r1-fixes candidate for 3.4) on the same table, and the full-cost delta in dollars. Results: runs/<run>/results/<arm>-r<n>-fix.json (loss hash, row sha, prompt sha, brief sha, base commit, cell HEAD, diffstat, agent outcome, spend, candidate id or void reason), ledger rows with arm `direct-fix`/`loop-fix`.
over: A baseline run outside the evaluator (an operator session by hand — unequal launch path, unrecorded spend, no sandbox); handing the baseline the loss as prose the operator writes (not the same row, not verbatim); a cell cloned from the live repo with its refs (the comparator branch reachable by `git log --all`); a best-of-N pick among baseline reps by hidden-test score (test-set selection, the thing 4.1 exists to forbid); charging the baseline only the loop's fix-session cost (the loop's detector and replay machinery would be free, the audit's finding 7); a score-per-dollar exchange rate to fold cost into the verdict (an invented constant — equal budget puts cost on the input side instead); letting the arms iterate on evaluator scores mid-session (hidden-answer feedback).
because: D1 keeps a change only if it beats the equal-budget direct-fix baseline net of the full improvement cost, and the audit's finding 7 asks for a matched-budget SIMPLER baseline. "Matched" is only checkable when both arms run through one launch path with every parameter recorded and one ledger charging every attempt (D12), and "full cost" is only honest when the loop's out-of-evaluator spend is stated on the baseline's input side rather than estimated on the output side. Hiding the comparator by exporting a commit into a refless repo costs nothing and closes the git route; the kernel closes the filesystem route (D9 §3); the transcript scan is the measured limit of what remains. Reading the approved row from the record makes approval (2.3) the only door into a fix cycle for the loop and the baseline alike.
